answer: Forced-Divergence Challenge. Each identity periodically receives a unique, randomly seeded puzzle whose answer depends on its private history. Clones share history, so they cannot produce divergent answers. Solving costs compute and a small nectar fee; a clone catching up must pay the full cost again from scratch. Honest identities spread across the meadow cheaply, while a sybil farm's identical answers expose it and its timber of accounts gets culled.
